title: The Rock's Surprising New Gig: Singing a Tender Ballad for His Daughters
summary:
Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson has conquered the wrestling ring and the box office. Now, he's setting his sights on the music charts with a surprisingly tender ballad called 'Your Dad.' The song, co-written with 2023 American Idol winner Iam Tongi, appears on the new album 'Moana: Voices Across the Ocean,' a companion to the live-action Moana reboot.

The track is a heartfelt ode to his three daughters: Simone (24), Jasmine (10), and Tiana (8). The music video features home movies of Johnson doting on his girls. In a whispery voice over gentle acoustic guitar, he sings, 'Now you go move those mountains / And sail across the oceans / Go show the world and prove / There's nothing you can't do.'

Johnson, known for his bulging biceps and action-hero roles, has dabbled in music before — he provided shout-outs on a Wyclef Jean song in 2000 and sang 'You're Welcome' in the original Moana. But this is his first full-fledged musical pivot. He told Rolling Stone that singing is in his blood: 'Growing up, in our family, and generally in Polynesian families, there is a lot of singing and there's a lot of ceremonial dancing.' He also cited influences like Sam Cooke, Elvis, and Willie Nelson, who actually gave him one of only 100 replicas of his famous 'Trigger' guitar.

The song's origin is touching. Tongi originally wrote it about his late father, but Johnson asked to rework it to focus on his daughters. Johnson said he cried when he first heard it, especially the part where Tongi sings about telling his future kids about their amazing grandfather. Johnson's own relationship with his late father, wrestler Rocky Johnson, was 'complicated,' so he wanted a song that celebrated his bond with his girls.

For Johnson, this song is personal, not commercial. 'There's no pressure of an expectation to deliver something that, 'Well, how are the sales, and how's the box office?' It's just from me to them,' he said. It's a sweet, unexpected side of a tough guy — and proof that even The Rock has a soft spot for his kids.
why_it_matters: Johnson's turn to heartfelt music reveals that even larger-than-life celebrities can use art to express private emotions—a reminder that vulnerability and fame aren't opposites.

background_read: Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson (a former professional wrestler turned Hollywood superstar, one of the highest-grossing actors ever) is best known for action films like the 'Fast & Furious' series and 'Jumanji.'

The original 'Moana' (a 2016 Disney animated film set in Polynesian mythology) was a massive hit that introduced a new generation to Pacific Island music and storytelling; a live-action reboot is now in the works.
Iam Tongi (the winner of American Idol season 21 in 2023) moved audiences with his emotional tribute to his late father during the competition, a theme that carries directly into 'Your Dad.'
Willie Nelson (the country music legend, now 92, known for his iconic guitar 'Trigger') is one of Johnson's musical heroes, making the gift of a replica guitar a deeply meaningful gesture.

perspectives.description: Fans see a softer, more relatable side of Johnson. The song humanizes an action hero, and the emotional music video strengthens his bond with audiences who value family-first messages.

Some critics might view the song as a calculated publicity move to soften his image or cross-promote the new Moana album. They question whether a ballad from a non-singer is genuine artistry or celebrity overreach.

The song reflects a long tradition of public figures using music for personal tribute. Johnson's explanation about Polynesian family singing also highlights how cultural heritage can shape artistic expression beyond commercial genres.

If the song is well-received, it could open the door for more actors to release personal music projects, blurring the line between film and music industries. However, it also risks setting a trend where celebrity status overshadows musical skill.
